svg.aria-label: Budlum Leaf plate P05 link multipath and fail-safe
svg.title: BUDLUM LEAF · P05 LINK, MULTIPATH AND FAIL-SAFE
svg.text: BUDLUM LEAF · P05 · LINK, MULTIPATH AND FAIL-SAFE
The compute is not in the device. Therefore the link is not a feature of Budlum Leaf: the link is the product. A bad link is a screen and a battery that do not work.
A · WHAT THE LINK MUST CARRY, AND THE PHYSICS THAT SETS IT

g.text: light in fibre travels about 200 km per millisecond. a round trip of 1 000 km costs about 10 ms before any routing delay.
the validator must stand close to the user. that is a siting requirement, not a software trick.
a data centre within 200 km is required for a round trip under 10 ms. an edge node 10 to 15 km away is measured at 1 to 5 ms.
9 000 km across a continent is 100 to 200 ms. the product states the class it is in, and never a promise.
report the class per market. "always connected" is a forbidden phrase.

svg.text: B · THE RADIO SET · and the five ways this architecture fights it

g.text: Wi-Fi 7 tri-band, multi-link operation, 320 MHz channels, two streams minimum and four preferred
5G standalone, sub-6 GHz, 4x4 MIMO, carrier aggregation
mmWave antenna in package, a standard 4x4 dual-polarised block, about 15 by 15 mm for one band
satellite non-terrestrial through the same cellular radio: no extra antenna
GNSS · Bluetooth for the wallet authenticator · NFC for the tap · ultra-wideband as a candidate
the antennas are printed along the leaf edges, dual-polarised, with windows through the core
THE MODULE IS A SECOND ANTENNA SITE. a module on the far edge is a diversity path, and a detached module is a relay on the body.

svg.text: THE FIVE CONFLICTS THAT MUST BE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED

g.text: 1 · the core sits between the antennas, so the antenna windows are holes in the core and in the anchor layer
2 · the metal anchor layer is close to the antennas: it is patterned for exactly this reason
3 · upright B stem antenna stands clear of the body: measure MIMO isolation and hand phantom effects
4 · the bend changes the geometry, so the antenna match is measured flat and at the qualification radius
5 · the module magnet may sit over an antenna: measure the gain loss, then set the keep-out
an attach that costs 3 dB is worse than a mechanical clip. G-H10 decides.

svg.text: C · THE MEASURED STATE OF THE TECHNOLOGIES, 2026

g.text: 2.5 ms to 7.1 ms, below 10 ms at all densities
8 to 12 ms in the field, 30 ms in early builds
edge server near a base station
about 14 ms total, 1.8 ms of jitter
1 to 5 ms near, 50 to 100 ms at a central cloud
about 650 satellites, 20 to 40 ms, 4 Mbit/s per user
150 Mbit/s peak per user, 120 Mbit/s per satellite

svg.text: THE HONEST CONCLUSION. In a city with an edge node this is a real-time device. In a rural area with one path it is a delta-mode device.
In a dead zone with only a satellite it is a message device. The product states the class. It does not promise the city everywhere.
the measurement set is never a mean alone: throughput, round trip, jitter, loss, and the 99th percentile, per path and per class.
D · MANY PATHS AT ONCE · and the choice of the validator

g.text: EVERY PATH AT THE SAME TIME · Wi-Fi, cellular, the satellite path through the cellular radio, and the Budlum network.
USE THE STANDARD MECHANISMS, DO NOT INVENT A TRANSPORT: multipath TCP and multipath QUIC above the IP layer,
with the steering, switching and splitting policy that the carrier core also understands. The 3GPP Release 16
architecture and its QUIC extension are the reference.
DUPLICATE THE CRITICAL PATH. The input uplink and the wallet messages are small, so they go twice over two paths
when the link is unstable. The cost is small and the gain is a removed stall.
THE VALIDATOR IS CHOSEN, NOT OWNED. Trust is the first filter, then latency, bandwidth, cost and energy.
It is a server choice, like a content delivery network, and it is reversible.

svg.text: WHAT A VALIDATOR AT ANY DISTANCE NEEDS · already resident in the Budlum tree

g.text: a persistent identity: the peer-to-peer layer and the DHT
network traversal: relay and STUN, exactly what the Mobile Self profile of a mobile node uses
encryption end to end, and a relayer that carries a signed transaction without holding a key
bandwidth: a home line is often asymmetric, an edge node or a data centre is not

svg.text: E · THE FAIL-SAFE LADDER · the device is never a brick
THE LOCAL FLOOR · hardware, not software

g.text: the safe screen, the wallet approval, the input echo and
the battery state are local functions in the keep-out
band, with no second path. this is rule H11.
THE OPTICAL PATH · the tree already carries it: B.U.D. has a
QR and receipt line, and the note-packing crate defines one
packing for the privacy note, with compressed and encrypted
payloads and deterministic QR frames. so the no-link state
has a physical transfer channel: show a signed receipt or a
small payload as optical frames and let the other device
read it. no radio at all. this is work order RG-12.
the ladder is measured: a session never enters a stuck state (G-L4, G-H19).
G-H10 the radio set, the antennas and the input: efficiency and pattern in a free hold and a hand hold, the desense between
the radios, the module magnet effect, the anchor layer effect, the match flat and bent, the gesture and gaze rates.
G-L1 Wi-Fi 7 and the fallback · G-L4 the link cut · G-L7 multi-path switching · G-H23 the module as a radio path.
REPORT BL14 · the link report: the classes, the multi-path result, the fail-safe ladder and the latency per distance.
REPORT BL6 · the radio and interaction report, including the module as a carrier of a second antenna site.
